messages.author: 91608aa139338355
messages.subject: Missing data: impute or ignore?
parts:
Thanks to the moderators and contributers for making this forum very
helpful!

Here's my particular problem...

I'm using distsamp and I have a single species surveyed in 2 parks.
Detection covariates and certain topographical variables (elevation,
slope) can be modeled across the 2 sites and a park effect wasn't
supported on detection or certain density variables.

My issue is that I would like to map density and distribution and I
have separate (non-overlapping) landcover layers for each park - which
results in ~400 "NA"s for habitat categories in one park or the other
(habitat types treated as columns - proportion of a cell size
consisting of that habitat type).

R wants to discard all of the observations that don't pertain to a
particular park - which is biasing my detection and common
covariates.

I tried various ways to get R to retain the NAs, but failed. So, I
thought I might impute 0s for the NAs and then include park and
interaction terms (ignoring the coefs that don't make sense).

The main reason I don't like this method is because it doubles the
number of parameters (from ~25 to 50) and slows everything down,
despite including initial values and running models without SE
calculations.

Is there a way to make unmarked ignore the NAs instead of discarding
the rows? Alternatively, is there a way I could format the model to
only estimate density for a certain park?

Thanks! C-

messages.author: 057bfe4d4b636b43
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Missing data: impute or ignore?
parts:
Hi,

I don't know if this fully addresses your question, but if you are
using a covariate in an unmarked model, it has to be in all of the
rows used to form the likelihood. Same thing with simple linear
regression. One cannot create a sensible design matrix without having
values for everything. You could try to impute values via a model
(either with unmarked or BUGS, Andy Royle and Marc Kery have distance
sampling models in the ecology examples section in OpenBUGS that could
be easily extended to include missing covariates). You may have to
simply do models for each park (and inference would not be able to
extend outside of that park), or truncate the available covariates to
those that are available across all of your data, potentially severely
limiting the available model sets. Not a fun trade-off, but I pretty
much run into this problem everyday, especially with GIS covariate
layers.

For estimating in a single park, couldn't you subset the data before
creating the unmarked data object? For example:

park1data = subset(parkdata, park=1)

Matthew

messages.subject: Re: Missing data: impute or ignore?
parts:
If I understand correctly, it is the multiple categorical landcover covariates that have missing data?   It seems that you could rerun the model with only the data from one park.  Alternatively you could crosswalk the landcover types -- i.e. perhaps meadow-shrub is equivalent to Sage-grassland? Is this what you mean by impute?

Best,
Tabitha Graves

Thanks everyone -

After thinking about it, I don't think what I wanted to do makes sense
from the design matrix perspective (thanks Matthew). I want the
detection covariates to apply to data across parks, but some density
covariates to be park specific, essentially - so I think I'll have to
set nonsensical values to 0 and include interactions in the abundance
models. A landcover crosswalk is in the works, but not ready yet,
unfortunately.
